locator: I-II q.94 a.4 co.: apud omnes enim hoc rectum est et verum, ut secundum rationem agatur
interpretation: In practical matters there is 'veritas vel rectitudo practica', the same for all as to the common principles; a proper conclusion such as 'deposits are to be returned' is 'verum ut in pluribus' and can fail in a case, that is, be not right and not true there. Read as: moral judgments have a truth value. Only truth-aptness is formalized, not which judgments are true or how widely they are known.
